body:
> 14.1.3 - Verify that server configuration is hardened as per the recommendations of the application server and frameworks in use.

[Live version](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v141-build-and-deploy)
[Point in time version](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/cda75733b1f8740a64db1a6241bd48e402dbb6e3/5.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md#v141-build-and-deploy)

This requirement feels unsuited to more dynamic applications which might be more cloud or microservice oriented. I would suggest changing this to:

> 14.1.3 - Verify that configuration hardening is performed on all 3rd party products, libraries, frameworks and services as per their individual recommendations.

Thoughts? Feedback?

comments.body:
And if you read this requirement, what precisely you going to check? I think we don't need this abstract requirement at all and we need to cover this with requirements like:
> V1.14.7 [MOVED FROM 1.2.1] Verify the use of unique or special low-privilege operating system accounts for all application components, services, and servers.
This is more like a process thing, making sure that for each component they have a process of ensuring they are using a hardened configuration. To me, V1.14.7 is too specific for this case.

when I think of server configuration I think of the parent components that enable services to run and then perform its function, talking about least privilege accounts is out of sync here, it’s the right thing to say but wrong place, I would go with ‘ensure hosting components are compliant’ this opens up a conversation with what that looks like if it doesn’t exist or how it should be if it does exist
Agree with @tghosth's proposed change here. Much better

I had a chance to this this over more and I think it should go.

_13.4.5 | Verify that configuration hardening is performed on all third-party products, libraries, frameworks, and services as per their individual recommendations._

The problems are:

- Vague ("per vendor guidance" varies wildly)
- Not testable without deep vendor config docs
- Can devolve into “did you read the manual?”

Previous discussion https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2703#issuecomment-2725949574

I agree, it is vague and not that clearly verifiable.

It could also be argued that it is more of a process than a specific requirement.

I'd support removal. @elarlang can you PR and update mapping?

> It could also be argued that it is more of a process than a specific requirement.

It is something you get done via process, but it is not a requirement to dictate that you need to use a process or how to achieve that.

Although the requirement is vague and can not be that clear how to verify that - as it depends on used 3rd party - it is a requirement I have used during pen-test report to point out - there is a clear guideline how to harden the configuration for the used component by the vendor and it should be followed.

Based on that, and following the move from #2953, maybe we should move this one to recommendation as well?

>  maybe we should move this one to recommendation as well?

Makes sense to me, will you open a PR on that basis?

Probably it is a new or separate topic, but we don't have a clear requirement to say that every application component must have permission to do only those things that are required for the application to do? For example, having reading/writing permissions only for files and folders that are necessary?

We have such a requirement for communication:
> 13.2.2	Verify that communications between backend application components, including local or operating system services, APIs, middleware, and data layers, are performed with accounts assigned the least necessary privileges.

But nothing for OS? Or the requirement covers the needs, just the section used ("communications") does not match that well?

> Probably it is a new or separate topic, but we don't have a clear requirement to say that every application component must have permission to do only those things that are required for the application to do? For example, having reading/writing permissions only for files and folders that are necessary?

Do you want to open a separate issue on that?
This is all a very positive direction. 👍🏼
